chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When the child reaches five palms (in height), his slaughtered animal is eaten.'

key_terms.الصَّبِيُّ: child (specifically a young boy in this context)
key_terms.خَمْسَةَ أَشْبَارٍ: five palms (a traditional unit of measurement for height)
key_terms.ذَبِيحَتُهُ: his slaughtered animal (the meat he has slaughtered)

ai.seo_question: At what age or height is a child's slaughter of an animal considered valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the minimum physical maturity for a child's *dhabihah* (slaughter) to be valid, using the measurement of five *ashbar* (palms) as the threshold. In Shia jurisprudence, this physical benchmark serves as a proxy for the child's developing capacity to understand and perform the essential acts of slaughter, distinguishing it from the stricter requirements of *tamyiz* (discernment) often required for other legal acts.
